priority.group: Priority assigned by the workspace’s default study, shown for every study as a baseline. Your own study’s ratings are under “This research study”.

options.P1: Work to start next. Example: prepare an important lab-mapping reference or resolve one CLL access route. A P1 dataset can still be incomplete.
options.P2: Potentially useful after we identify a specific gap. Example: another hospital dataset might add a new schema. We should establish that need before downloading it.
options.Maintain: Keep using the existing, approved subset for its recorded purpose. No expansion or new acquisition is currently prioritized.
options.P3 / hold: Defer acquisition for now. The source may be useful later, but it does not address the current benchmark's most important gaps. This does not mean the dataset is poor quality.

ready.group: Whether the currently held files can support the recorded development task. This is separate from whether a paper used the source, and from independent clinical benchmark validity.

options.ready_scoped: A specific set of prepared source files passed the recorded file, table-reading and local AI permission checks. Example: the MIMIC demo source subset. It does not clear the entire parent database or certify clinical correctness.
options.needs_preparation_or_permissions: Some files are held, but something must be resolved before the intended use: an adapter, source/reference separation, labels, permissions or another preparation step. Open the dataset's problems section for the actual blocker.
options.incomplete: A necessary part is missing, such as a dictionary, target list, expert reference, patient file or access agreement. This does not necessarily mean the files we have are damaged.
options.reference_only: Useful supporting material is held, such as terminology, schema documentation or conversion code. It is not a ready participant-level extraction input.
options.not_appropriate: Excluded from the current primary clinical benchmark objective, for example because it is redundant or tests a different task. It may still have value elsewhere.

available.group: Which files the project already holds, shared by every study, and when they were obtained. Holding a file is not permission to use it; see “Permission for intended local AI use”. Discovery downloads nothing.

options.selected subset held: The selected data or reference files are held and hash-verified. This is not a claim that the full provider release is present.
options.partial package: Some relevant parts are present, while others are missing. Example: prepared clinical tables are held, but original workbooks or required reference mappings are absent.
options.metadata / code / reference only: We have descriptions, dictionaries, code, standards or reference material, rather than a complete participant-data package. Such material can still be valuable for metadata mapping.
options.not acquired: No usable dataset payload is assigned to this entry in the verified inventory. A paper or access webpage may still be known.

access.group: How new or full access would be obtained. Some entries combine an open demo with a controlled full database; a registration flag can therefore coexist with a ready demo subset.

options.public_no_registration: The recorded source route is public and does not require an account. Its licence and AI-use conditions still apply.
options.registration: An account, training, study approval or agreement is required for new/full access. Example: full eICU access requires credentials even though its demo is open.
options.owner: Contact the authors, institution or data owner for permission or a shareable package. Example: request a small expert-labelled dictionary rather than patient records.
options.public_review: A public download or repository is a lead, but the exact files, suitability or conditions need review before acquisition.
options.unresolved: The exact access route has not been established adequately. Do not interpret this as either open access or a confirmed prohibition.

benchmark.group: What published studies report doing with the resource or its source family. This does not prove that our exact downloaded release or demo was evaluated in that paper.

options.mapping: Reported use in matching variables, clinical terms, schemas or ontologies. Example: a source dictionary mapped to expert-selected target concepts. Read the linked study relationship to check the exact version and scope.
options.extraction: Reported use in finding or retrieving clinical information from source records, such as evaluating an EHR extraction agent. This does not certify our own extraction workflow.
options.prediction: Reported use in predicting outcomes or evaluating learned patient/table representations. A prediction benchmark is useful context, but is different from a mapping benchmark with expert reference answers.
options.context: The register contains source, related-method or other contextual evidence, without a classified mapping/extraction/prediction evaluation use. A citation alone is not counted as benchmark validation.

kind.group: The broad category assigned in the project inventory. Combine it with availability to distinguish a source's subject matter from what is actually downloaded.

options.clinical_sources: Clinical source tables or related selected clinical exports. They may contain patient, visit, laboratory or treatment information. Held scope varies by entry.
options.mapping_references: Variable dictionaries, term lists, reference mappings or related benchmark material. Many mapping tasks can be tested without patient rows.
options.synthetic_controls: Generated data or software-control packages used to test processing behavior. Successful tests here do not establish validity on real clinical records.
options.tabular_controls: General tabular prediction inputs, such as ARFF tables. They can stress table-reading behavior but usually lack independent harmonization/extraction reference answers.
options.standards_and_methods: Standards, terminology, target catalogues, transformation recipes or ETL code. These support workflow components rather than serving as complete patient-level benchmarks.
options.metadata_only: Documentation or study metadata is held. The participant package or complete paired analysis input is absent.
options.pending_access: A candidate requiring access or an owner request. The intended package still needs checking; this category does not imply that any records are held.
options.excluded: An excluded or unsuitable control for the current primary clinical benchmark. Check the dataset record for the reason.

license.group: Licence families found in source-bound evidence, not permissions granted by this browser. A resource can have several component licences and unresolved parts. Software licensing does not automatically cover data.

options.attribution: A recorded data component uses an attribution licence such as CC BY. Credit and other applicable conditions remain required; separate vocabulary or provider conditions may still apply.
options.sharealike: A recorded component uses ODbL or related share-alike terms. Attribution and obligations for adapted databases need review before publishing derived datasets.
options.permissive: An applicable recorded data component uses MIT, Apache or BSD-style terms. Software-only licences are excluded from this filter, and unresolved inherited terms remain unknown.
options.public_domain: Recorded evidence identifies CC0 or public-domain material for a component. This does not extend to separately copyrighted terminology or other files in the package.
options.custom: The component has source-specific or terminology terms, such as LOINC/UCUM conditions or instrument restrictions. Read the exact rules rather than assuming a standard open licence.
options.dua: A public provider/data-use agreement has been screened for the access route. It is not a signed project agreement or permission to use the data. The same entry may also be marked unresolved.
options.unknown: The exact data/component grant is missing, unresolved or not tied to reviewed file identities. A paper's or repository's software licence cannot fill that gap.
options.restricted_cc: The recorded Creative Commons terms include noncommercial or no-derivatives restrictions. Read the exact licence and intended operation; this is not plain CC BY or blanket AI permission.

work.group: Specific kinds of work remaining. These flags can overlap. A source can be ready for narrow development while still needing independent benchmark reference review.

options.preparation: Prepare consistent input tables or a reader (adapter) for the provider's file format. Separate expected answers from source columns, and finish the recorded preparation or permission steps.
options.missing: Obtain or clarify a missing component, such as an expert answer set, dictionary, candidate release or necessary clinical table.
options.rights: The local AI permission check for the files associated with this entry is not allowed in the recorded snapshot. This can be missing rights/evidence rather than an explicit AI ban; an exact prepared subset may have a separate outcome.
options.registration: Complete the justified account, training or approval route for new/full access. This does not mean every held demo file needs registration.
options.owner: Ask an author or data owner for terms, a minimal shareable package or an authorized evaluation arrangement.
options.reference: Review expert answers and freeze an independent test split before claiming benchmark performance. Gold answers must not enter discovery prompts or tuning inputs.
options.format: A retained artifact has a recorded format problem, explicit issue or outstanding format review. Report the finding first; it is not permission to silently alter provider data.

relevance.group: Relevance judged by the workspace’s default study, shown for every study as a baseline. Your own study’s ratings are under “This research study”.

options.high: Directly supports a target task, such as clinical variable mapping, blood-laboratory context or an expert reference benchmark.
options.moderate: Potentially supports a useful component or a conditional follow-up. A specific new capability should justify preparation or acquisition.
options.low: Limited fit for the current primary clinical benchmark, such as a generic control or a different data modality.
options.unassessed: Source-specific evidence is not yet sufficient to establish useful additional capability. Inspect the metadata before deciding to download.

cll.group: How the source relates to chronic lymphocytic leukaemia (CLL) and the CLL-TIM task. A CLL cohort does not necessarily contain the required blood tests, dates or targets.

options.direct: A CLL study or cohort source. Verify its actual laboratory, treatment and time coverage before using it for CLL-TIM validation.
options.indirect: Supports laboratory names, units, clinical extraction or related context, but is not itself an established CLL-TIM validation cohort.
options.other: No direct CLL-TIM cohort relationship is established. The resource may still be useful for general harmonization.

format.group: File formats actually present among the associated retained or prepared artifacts. An archive or document is not evidence of usable patient rows inside it.

options.csv: Delimited tables such as CSV/TSV, including their compressed forms. Check the row, column, type and missing-value profiles before workflow use.
options.excel: Excel workbooks. They may have multiple sheets, merged headings, legends or formatting that an adapter must handle explicitly.
options.json: JSON, JSONL or NDJSON files. These can contain nested structures, metadata or mappings rather than flat clinical tables.
options.xml: XML or FHIR-related files. Structured records may require a format-specific reader and a verified mapping to the workflow's inputs.
options.clinical_binary: Native statistical formats such as SAS, Stata, SPSS or R data files. The correct reader, variable labels and missing-value meanings need checking.
options.arff: Attribute-Relation File Format, commonly used by ML benchmarks. Declared attributes and prediction targets are different from a harmonization reference answer set.
options.archive: A ZIP, tarball or compressed package is held. This filter does not certify the contents or imply that all members have been prepared.
options.document: PDF, Word, text or other documentation. This may include dictionaries, licences or expert references; it is not automatically participant data.
options.code: Scripts, notebooks or queries are held. Code can document a transformation, but is not the same as having its source data or validated output.
options.ontology: An ontology or terminology representation, such as OWL, OBO or RDF. Exact release and component terms matter for candidate matching.
options.other: A retained format outside the categories above. Open the artifact's format profile to see its actual type and validation limits.
options.not_held: No associated retained or prepared file format is available for this entry. A provider may advertise formats that we have not acquired.

size_retained.group: Size of associated retained source artifacts, including compressed archives, documentation or code. This is not the provider's full database size. Lower bounds are inclusive and upper bounds exclusive.

options.lt1: Less than 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes). A small dictionary or mapping reference can be very useful even at this size.
options.1to10: At least 1 MiB and less than 10 MiB of associated retained artifacts.
options.10to100: At least 10 MiB and less than 100 MiB of associated retained artifacts.
options.100to1024: At least 100 MiB and less than 1 GiB (1,024 MiB) of associated retained artifacts.
options.gte1024: At least 1 GiB of associated retained artifacts. Size alone is not a measure of usefulness or participant count.
options.unknown: No retained size is established for this entry. Unknown is kept separate from zero; tick it together with other bands if you want both.

size_prepared.group: Size of prepared representations associated with the entry. These copies are counted separately from retained provider artifacts. Lower bounds are inclusive and upper bounds exclusive.

options.lt1: Less than 1 MiB in prepared representations, such as a small normalized dictionary or source-only table.
options.1to10: At least 1 MiB and less than 10 MiB in prepared representations.
options.10to100: At least 10 MiB and less than 100 MiB in prepared representations.
options.100to1024: At least 100 MiB and less than 1 GiB in prepared representations.
options.gte1024: At least 1 GiB in prepared representations. This is a storage measure, not a benchmark-quality score.
options.unknown: No prepared size is established. This usually means the needed representation has not been prepared or assigned, rather than that the provider dataset is empty.

size_provider.group: Size of a specific provider-advertised artifact when verified evidence is recorded, including not-yet-downloaded packages. This is not automatically the full database, minimal requested subset or extra storage needed.

options.lt1: A verified advertised artifact smaller than 1 MiB. Its exact package scope and evidence are recorded in the dataset details.
options.1to10: A verified advertised artifact at least 1 MiB and smaller than 10 MiB. This may be metadata rather than participant records.
options.10to100: A verified advertised artifact at least 10 MiB and smaller than 100 MiB. Its provider package may still need file-level and licence review before download.
options.100to1024: A verified advertised artifact at least 100 MiB and smaller than 1 GiB. This is not an estimate of a full cohort unless the recorded scope explicitly says so.
options.gte1024: A verified advertised artifact of at least 1 GiB. Check the release, file list, relevance and permitted minimal subset before considering a large transfer.
options.unknown: No provider/package byte size is verified in the current evidence. This is unknown, not zero. Request the exact file manifest rather than estimating from a paper or dictionary.

license_status.group: Permission is separate from download completeness, licence family and technical readiness. Approved means a recorded exact local AI scope passes the lenient snapshot; source review alone cannot clear unidentified inputs.

options.approved: The documented local source scope passed its recorded local inference/embedding checks. Read the exact file scope and conditions; other releases and remote providers remain separate.
options.source_reviewed: A manual source review has been registered, but exact held input identities are not yet cleared. Plan a reviewed download and bind its delivery before inference.
options.review_required: Underlying rights, evidence, release coverage or AI permission remain unresolved. Read the attached notice and record a manual review or seek clarification.
options.prohibited: An applicable recorded restriction blocks the intended local AI operation. A manual click cannot override the prohibition or replace a missing agreement.

project_relevance.group: Your relevance assessment is scoped to the active research project, independent of the default study’s baseline ratings.

options.high: Highly useful for this research question, as annotated by the user or reviewed intake. This is not a licence or benchmark-quality clearance.
options.moderate: Potentially useful for some aspects of this study, with the reasoning retained in the per-study annotation.
options.low: Limited fit for the current research study; this does not remove it from the shared catalogue or other projects.
options.unassessed: No relevance annotation has been made for this research study. Unknown relevance must not be treated as high or low.

project_role.group: The intended use is a study-specific annotation. Benchmark candidate does not mean independently validated benchmark-ready.

options.development: Proposed for workflow development or optimization in this study, separately from independent held-out evaluation.
options.benchmark: Proposed benchmark candidate for this study; rights, completeness, reference correctness and frozen splits still need independent checks.
options.reference: Useful as documentation, context, dictionaries or supporting reference material for this study.
options.exclude: The user marked it outside this study’s selection. Files and historical evidence remain in the shared catalogue.
options.unassessed: No intended-role annotation has been recorded for this research study yet.

project_tags.group: Topic tags come from dataset annotations for this research study. Custom tags appear after saving an annotation; several tags within this group match any selected tag.

options.untagged: No topic tag has been saved for this dataset in the current research project.

study_shortlist.group: Shortlists are separate for each research project and can be exported with its brief and annotations. Saving a shortlist grants no download or data-use rights.

options.shortlisted: This catalogue ID is saved in the active research study’s shortlist in this browser or imported profile.
options.not_shortlisted: This catalogue ID has not been saved in the active research study’s shortlist.

review_route.group: This describes how licensing was reviewed or what remains to be done. Always combine it with the separate permission-status filter; an old manual decision can expire or record a prohibition.

options.evidence_reviewed: The recorded exact scope passes its licensing evidence checks, with no manual-review importer record for this study. This is not an automated legal guarantee.
options.manual_required: The current intended study use needs licence evidence, manual interpretation or provider clarification. It is not proof of an explicit AI ban.
options.manual_recorded: A human decision was registered for this study. Read its status and scope: it may be an approval, a prohibition or a request for clarification.

blocker.group: Why an entry is not ready, shown under its readiness state. Several reasons can apply. Open the dataset’s “Problems & next steps” for the exact wording.

options.prep_rights: The project’s local AI permission check for the files associated with this entry is not allowed in the recorded snapshot: rights or evidence are missing, or a condition is unresolved. Downloading does not change this.
options.prep_reference: A candidate benchmark whose expected answers still need independent reference review and a frozen train/test split before any evaluation claim.
options.prep_control: Held as a software or tabular control resource; it is not independent clinical gold and cannot certify clinical mapping or extraction correctness.
options.prep_version: The held files differ from the version, counts or snapshot described in the source paper or provider documentation, or a recorded component is absent or empty.
options.prep_format: A held file failed the recorded structure check or has format issues that a reader or adapter must resolve before use.
options.prep_adapter: The recorded notes ask for a reader/adapter, sheet- or column-level separation of references from source values, or a reconciliation step before the task can run.
options.prep_access: A registration, data-use agreement or owner approval is still needed for the files this task requires.
options.inc_access: A registration, credentialed access, data-use agreement, author request or institutional approval is outstanding according to the access route or the recorded notes.
options.inc_licence: The applicable licence or terms are not stated, not retrievable, not verified or not yet reviewed for this study; rights cannot be inferred.
options.inc_reference: A dictionary, target list, expert labels, gold mappings, splits or another reference component is missing according to the recorded notes.
options.inc_records: Participant files, patient-level records, cohort snapshots or the actual source tables are not held; public dictionaries do not substitute for them.
options.inc_identity: Exact files, hashes, manifest, size, version or provenance are not verified, or overlaps with other entries are not reconciled.
options.inc_other: The recorded gap did not match any of the categories above; read the dataset's problem notes for the specific missing part.
